first.rationale: Two of the three live signals (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) point at funnel health, and funnel repair compounds into durable qualified revenue rather than buying one-off volume, so simplify_onboarding is the current intent. Verification budget goes to the two beliefs that are both decisive here and thinnest against the stated objective. memory_86 is the direct load-bearing justification for the intended action, but as recorded it only establishes completion rate and time-to-value lift plus 'early product adoption' — none of which is demonstrated to carry through to retained, qualified revenue; shortened onboarding can also lift completion by admitting lower-intent accounts, so I need the original record's downstream metrics, holdout design, and horizon. memory_73 is the belief most likely to hijack this decision, since the competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing feel like the obvious counter, and the memory claims 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' while saying nothing about margin, discount cohort retention, or whether the lift persisted after promo expiry — a discount war against a cheaper entrant is precisely where short-horizon evidence misleads on long-term revenue. I deliberately do not spend budget on memory_31 (it duplicates the onboarding thesis and already claims durability, so it is redundant with memory_86 for triage purposes), memory_91 (activation messaging is a plausible fallback but lower-consequence this week), memory_57 (referral incentives address neither live signal), or memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist does not address SMB price pressure or the activation drop). If memory_86's archived record shows the lift was measured only on completion with no revenue-side or multi-week follow-through, I will downgrade this to a guarded test with explicit qualified-revenue and retention endpoints, or shift to activation_messaging under memory_91. If memory_73 turns out to have clean post-promo retention and margin data, promotional_pricing becomes a live contender despite the structural discounting risk. All inherited claims are treated as provisional until the source records are read.

final.rationale: Both verifications resolved cleanly and in opposite directions, which settles the decision. exp_86 held up beyond the compressed metric I was worried about: completion +13% and time-to-value -2.1 days were accompanied by 30-day retention +3%, so the shortened flow was not merely admitting lower-intent accounts — the cohort it produced stuck. That is the downstream-value evidence the memory summary omitted, and it converts memory_86 from a funnel-metric claim into a defensible qualified-revenue claim. exp_73 collapsed in exactly the way the summary concealed: signup +31% and qualified revenue +18% were purchased with 30-day retention -12%, and the source record explicitly instructs against generalizing targeted discounting as sustainable growth. The consolidated memory line 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' was materially misleading by omission, and the competitor's entry pricing is precisely the pressure that would have made me act on it. I am committing to simplify_onboarding at standard experiment scale. It is the only candidate supported by verified retention-inclusive evidence, it addresses two of the three live signals directly (onboarding completion -4%, and activation -6% via improved time-to-value), and it answers the competitor threat on the durable axis — product value delivered faster — rather than on price, where we would lose the trade even when we win the signup. I explicitly decline promotional_pricing despite the competitive pressure; matching a cheaper entrant with discounts would import the exact cohort that fails at first renewal and would degrade long-term qualified revenue while appearing to work for a quarter. Residual uncertainty I am carrying rather than papering over: exp_86's retention readout is 30-day, which is shorter than a renewal cycle, so it does not prove the lift survives to renewal the way exp_73's failure proves the discount cohort does not; the original result also predates the current competitive environment and the day-76 funnel decline, whose cause is unverified — if the drop stems from traffic-mix shift toward price-shoppers rather than friction, onboarding repair will underperform. memory_31 is corroborating but unverified and I am leaning on it only lightly. I will therefore instrument this against qualified revenue and retention at 30 and 90 days with a holdout, not against completion rate alone, since completion is the metric most easily gamed by removing friction. If the retention arm goes flat or negative, I stop rather than scale. memory_91 (activation messaging) is my documented fallback for the next slot, and I am flagging that both memory_73 and memory_57 assert benign-retention outcomes in summary form while memory_73's source disproved it — memory_57's referral claim of 'no measurable harm to retention' should be treated as suspect and verified before anyone acts on it.
